title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 'second part' of La Longue Marche (variations on the loop equation, 'équation des lacets'). Pi_{0,3}^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}. M_{0,3}^{~} is a group of (outer) automorphisms of it, enlarged by the involution tau ('complex conjugation'). M_{0,3}^{!~} is the subgroup preserving the inertia conjugacy classes. On the previous page Grothendieck built a 'finer' central extension 1 -> Z^ -> S_0M^{!~} -> M^{!~} -> 1. Its elements are the pairs (u, f_0) with u(l_0) = int(f_0^{-1})(l_0^lambda), where lambda = chi(u). Pushing this extension out along the diagonal Z^ -> Z^3 gives the extension SM^{!~}.

This page makes S_0M^{!~} explicit, using the computations of §46 V. Pi_{0,3}^ is viewed inside G^_{0,3}, a profinite completion of a group of SL_2/PSL_2(Z) type, which is an amalgam generated by torsion elements rho and sigma.

- Parametrisation (16). Pairs (alpha, f_0 = f) are encoded by triples (alpha, beta, f):
  - alpha lies in Pi^{~^}, the inverse image of {1, tau} under G^_{0,3} -> T_{0,3}; this is Pi^ extended by the involution tau_infty.
  - beta and f lie in Pi^.
- The loop equation (17). The triples are subject to a relation not involving f: alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} = beta sigma(beta)^{-1} E_1(mu-1). Here rho(x) means conjugation by rho, so xi*rho = alpha rho alpha^{-1}. The correction factor is E_1(mu-1) = h^nu when mu-1 = 2 nu, with h the central element.
- The parameter mu. mu in Z^* is uniquely determined by alpha. It depends only on xi = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} computed in the image GL(2,Z^)^{±1}, i.e. matrices of determinant ±1. So mu is a cyclotomic-type character, the analogue of lambda = chi(u), read off from the congruence image.
- The case f = 1 (18). Triples with f = 1 give the subgroup of S_0M^{!~} identified with the normaliser of the inertia subgroup L_0 in M^{!~}, previously called M^{!~}[0].
- The automorphism u_{alpha,beta} (19)-(22). Setting xi = alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} and eta = beta sigma(beta)^{-1}, the automorphism is given by u(rho) = xi rho, u(sigma) = eta sigma. A general element is u_{alpha,beta,f} = int(f^{-1}) u_{alpha,beta}.
- The margin note says that to (u, f) one associates an element of M_{0,3} of the form u_{alpha,beta}.

Purpose: an explicit 'GT-type' description of the automorphism group of the profinite modular / three-point group, as solutions of a loop equation. On the next page this description is mapped to a congruence-level analogue SM_{rho,sigma}(Z^)' inside SL(2,Z^)-type data, satisfying the same loop relation.
errors: The relations are stated up to conventions ('ne pourrait dépendre comme associés ...' is hesitant). The claim that mu depends only on the GL_2(Z^) image of xi is asserted, not proved here; it is plausible since mu acts as the character on the abelianisation / inertia.
Minor notational inconsistency: (19) writes eta = beta phi(beta)^{-1} while (17) uses sigma. It is surely sigma.
No substantive mathematical error detectable on this page.

ideas.what: Describing automorphisms of the profinite three-point/modular group by pairs or triples (alpha, beta, f) subject to a 'loop equation' with a character mu in Z^*
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (pairs (lambda, f)) and its SL_2 / B_3 variants
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s); B_3/SL_2 versions: Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only alludes to the Teichmüller tower and SL_2(Z^) actions; La Longue Marche (circulated 1981) contains related material

ideas.what: Central extension S_0M of the inertia-preserving automorphism group by Z^, recording the conjugating element f; the subgroup f = 1 is the normaliser of the inertia subgroup L_0
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms of the profinite free group with a chosen tangential base point / 'special' (lambda, f) normalisation; normaliser of inertia

ideas.what: Reduction of the loop equation to the congruence quotient GL/SL(2,Z^), with mu read off from the image of alpha
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT^ / Galois in Aut of SL_2(Z^)-type quotients; cyclotomic character via congruence image
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in the GT literature (Ihara, Nakamura)

missed.claim: A variant of GT parametrised by triples (alpha, beta, f), with alpha in Pi^ extended by the complex-conjugation involution and the correction factor h^nu (nu = (mu-1)/2). This is a GT-like group built directly from the rho/sigma amalgam presentation of the modular group, including the involution, rather than from the free group on x, y. This specific normalisation does not match a standard published presentation, though its content is close to known GT/B_3 results.
missed.quote: alpha rho(alpha)^{-1} = beta sigma(beta)^{-1} E_1(mu-1), = h^nu si mu-1 = 2nu
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Offers an alternative parametrisation of GT^ including complex conjugation (a GT^± analogue) through the SL_2 amalgam. It may be of minor interest for comparing GT with Aut of the profinite completion of SL_2(Z) or B_3.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an intermediate computational page inside Grothendieck's unpublished development of a GT-type group via the loop equation. It is historically interesting as a pre-Drinfeld formulation, but the substance (GT-type parametrisation, normaliser of inertia, congruence image) is now standard. No clearly new finished result is visible on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'Pi_{0,3}^{~^} = Pi_{0,3}^ - {1, tau_infty}' is likely 'Pi_{0,3}^ · {1, tau_infty}', i.e. extended by the involution, consistent with 'image inverse de {1,tau}'.
'G^(1,Z^)^{±1}' is likely 'Gl(2,Z^)^{±1}', the image in GL_2 with determinant ±1.
The margin note probably reads: 'à (u,f) ↦ (u, f) ∈ M_{0,3}^{!~} est associé un élément de M_{0,3} de la forme u_{alpha beta}'.
Heading: 'S_0M_{0,3}^{!~}' continuation: '... de M_{0,3}^{!~} par Z^.'
